title: 正弦激励下 RL 电路的接通
statement: 图示电路中 v_s = 20 cos(100t) V，R = 10 Ω，L = 0.1 H，电感原来没有电流。开关 S 在 t = 0 时闭合（此时 v_s 正好处于正的最大值）。
求 v_L(0₊)、时间常数 τ、t = 0.01 s 时的电流 i，并讨论什么时刻合闸可以不出现过渡过程。

questions.explain: τ = L/R = 0.1/10 = 0.01 s，与激励的形式无关。

questions.ask: 若改为 v_s = 20 sin(100t + ψ) V，ψ 取何值时合闸后电流立即进入稳态（没有自由分量）？
choices: 任何 ψ 都会有过渡过程
choiceExplain: ψ = 0° 是电压过零时合闸，这对纯电阻电路才不产生过渡过程；RL 电路的稳态电流滞后电压一个角度，ψ = 0° 时 i_p(0₊) ≠ 0。
ψ = 90° 对应稳态电流滞后 90° 的纯电感电路；这里有 R = 10 Ω，电流滞后不到 90°，ψ = 90° 时 A = −1，仍有过渡过程（就是本题原来的情形）。
只要合闸瞬间稳态电流 i_p(0₊) 恰好等于 i(0₊) = 0，自由分量的系数就是 0，所以存在不出现过渡过程的 ψ。
questions.explain: 强制分量 i_p = √2 sin(100t + ψ − 45°)，自由分量 A e^(−100t) 的系数 A = i(0₊) − i_p(0₊) = −√2 sin(ψ − 45°)。ψ − 45° = 0 或 180° 时 A = 0，合闸瞬间稳态电流恰好为零，不出现过渡过程。

hints: 正弦激励的一阶电路：全响应 = 强制分量（正弦稳态解，用相量法求）+ 自由分量 A e^(−t/τ)。
相量法：Z = R + jωL = 10 + j10 = 10√2∠45° Ω。按余弦参考写振幅相量：v_s = 20 cos(100t) V → V̇_m = 20∠0° V。
常数 A 由 i(0₊) = 0 确定：A = 0 − i_p(0)。正弦激励没有“终值”，不能直接套用 f(∞) 的三要素公式。
solution: **6. 合闸相位。** 一般地 v_s = 20 sin(100t + ψ)：A = −√2 sin(ψ − 45°)。ψ = 45° 或 225° 时 A = 0，直接进入稳态；ψ = 135° 或 315° 时 |A| 最大（= √2 A），过渡过程最剧烈。
注意：正弦激励下电流没有终值 i(∞)，三要素法中的 f(∞) 要换成稳态解在 0₊ 的值 i_p(0₊)：i(t) = i_p(t) + [i(0₊) − i_p(0₊)]e^(−t/τ)。

en.title: Switching an RL circuit onto a sinusoidal source
statement: In the circuit, v_s = 20 cos(100t) V, R = 10 Ω, L = 0.1 H, and the inductor initially carries no current. Switch S closes at t = 0 (just when v_s is at its positive peak).
Find v_L(0+), the time constant τ, the current i at t = 0.01 s, and discuss when the switch should close so that there is no transient.

questions.explain: i(0+) = i(0−) = 0, so there is no drop across R: v_L(0+) = v_s(0) = 20 cos 0 = 20 V.
τ = L/R = 0.1/10 = 0.01 s, regardless of the type of source.

questions.ask: If instead v_s = 20 sin(100t + ψ) V, for which ψ does the current go straight into steady state when the switch closes (no natural component)?
choices: There is a transient for every ψ
choiceExplain: ψ = 0° closes the switch at a voltage zero, which avoids a transient only in a purely resistive circuit; in an RL circuit the steady current lags the voltage by some angle, so at ψ = 0° i_p(0+) ≠ 0.
ψ = 90° fits a purely inductive circuit, where the current lags by 90°; here R = 10 Ω makes the lag less than 90°, and ψ = 90° gives A = −1 — a transient (exactly the original case).
Whenever the steady-state current at the switching instant, i_p(0+), equals i(0+) = 0, the natural component's coefficient is zero, so such a ψ does exist.
questions.explain: The forced component is i_p = √2 sin(100t + ψ − 45°); the natural component A e^(−100t) has A = i(0+) − i_p(0+) = −√2 sin(ψ − 45°). For ψ − 45° = 0 or 180°, A = 0: the steady-state current happens to be zero at the switching instant, so there is no transient.

hints: First-order circuit with a sinusoidal source: complete response = forced component (the sinusoidal steady-state solution, found with phasors) + natural component A e^(−t/τ).
Phasors: Z = R + jωL = 10 + j10 = 10√2∠45° Ω. With the cosine reference the amplitude phasor of v_s = 20 cos(100t) V is V̇_m = 20∠0° V.
The constant A follows from i(0+) = 0: A = 0 − i_p(0). A sinusoidal source has no 'final value', so the f(∞) form of the three-element formula can't be used directly.
solution: **1. Initial values.** The inductor carries no current initially: i(0+) = 0, **v_L(0+) = v_s(0) = 20 V**.
**5. At t = 0.01 s.** 100t = 1 rad = 57.30°: i = √2 cos(12.30°) − e⁻¹ = 1.3818 − 0.3679 ≈ **1.014 A**. After about 5τ = 0.05 s the natural component is negligible and the current is a pure sinusoid.

**6. Switching phase.** In general, for v_s = 20 sin(100t + ψ): A = −√2 sin(ψ − 45°). For ψ = 45° or 225°, A = 0 and the circuit enters steady state immediately; for ψ = 135° or 315°, |A| is largest (√2 A) and the transient is strongest.

Note: with a sinusoidal source the current has no final value i(∞); in the three-element formula f(∞) is replaced by the steady-state solution and its value at 0+: i(t) = i_p(t) + [i(0+) − i_p(0+)]e^(−t/τ).
